channel.title: Nature Energy
channel.description: Nature Energy is an online-only journal interested in all aspects of energy, from its generation and storage, to its distribution and management, the needs and demands of the different actors involved, and the impacts that energy technologies and policies have on different societies. The journal has a particular interest in studies that advance our knowledge and inform the development of next-generation technologies and solutions. Nature Energy publishes research from the natural, behavioural and social sciences.

item.title: Amorphous self-assembled multilayers for perovskite solar cells with improved reverse bias stability
item.content:encoded:
Nature Energy, Published online: 20 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02015-8

The morphology of hole-selective contacts is key to the stability of perovskite solar cells. Feng et al. use self-assembled molecules with extended conjugation and hydroxyl groups to form dense, amorphous films that suppress degradation induced by ion migration.
item.dc:title: Amorphous self-assembled multilayers for perovskite solar cells with improved reverse bias stability

item.title: Alkali-metal-mediated control of phase segregation for flexible kesterite solar cells and modules with improved efficiency
item.content:encoded:
Nature Energy, Published online: 20 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02018-5

The incorporation of alkali metals in kesterite solar cells enables high efficiency but is challenging to control. Xu et al. show that combining Na and Li ions yields optimal phase formation, enabling efficient solar cells and modules.
item.dc:title: Alkali-metal-mediated control of phase segregation for flexible kesterite solar cells and modules with improved efficiency

item.title: Exploiting the insulator–metal transition of VO<sub>2</sub> in photocatalytic methane conversion
item.content:encoded:
Nature Energy, Published online: 17 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02013-w

Photocatalysts for methane conversion can suffer from inefficient charge carrier diffusion, limiting their effectiveness. Here the authors exploit the insulator–metal transition in VO2 to create an electronic phase junction, enhancing the non-oxidative conversion of methane into hydrogen, ethane and propane, with peak efficiency at the transition’s critical temperature.
item.dc:title: Exploiting the insulator–metal transition of VO<sub>2</sub> in photocatalytic methane conversion

item.title: Additive-assisted perovskite crystallization on industrial TOPCon silicon for tandem solar cells with improved efficiency
item.content:encoded:
Nature Energy, Published online: 16 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02010-z

Crystallizing the perovskite layer on thin tunnel oxide passivated contact silicon cells is challenging due to rapid heat transfer. Zhou et al. address this issue using a 2-mercaptobenzothiazole additive, achieving a tandem cell efficiency of 32.76%.
item.dc:title: Additive-assisted perovskite crystallization on industrial TOPCon silicon for tandem solar cells with improved efficiency

item.title: Irreversible organic cations chemistry limits organic–inorganic halide perovskite stability under illumination or bias
item.content:encoded:
Nature Energy, Published online: 13 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-01965-3

Oxidation and reduction reactions undermine the stability of perovskite solar cells under illumination and bias. In this Perspective, Ren et al. examine the impact of irreversible reactions involving organic cations, identify key knowledge gaps, and outline strategies for mitigation.
item.dc:title: Irreversible organic cations chemistry limits organic–inorganic halide perovskite stability under illumination or bias

item.title: Understanding UK public preferences and attitudes to a decarbonized heating system
item.content:encoded:
Nature Energy, Published online: 12 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-01978-y

Substantial heterogeneity is evident in stances towards the development of aquifer thermal energy storage (ATES) systems in the UK. An assessment of individual preferences reveals substantial valuations of specific ATES characteristics that are nevertheless modified by latent attitudes regarding systemic and local benefits, safety concerns, information provision, and policy support.
item.dc:title: Understanding UK public preferences and attitudes to a decarbonized heating system

item.title: Bifacial tunnel oxide passivating contacts for silicon and perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells with improved efficiency
item.content:encoded:
Nature Energy, Published online: 11 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02007-8

Interfacial charge recombination losses limit solar cell efficiency. Gao et al. mitigate these losses through front and rear-contact engineering, achieving efficiencies of 26.34% and 32.73% in tunnel oxide passivating contact single-junction and tandem solar cells.
item.dc:title: Bifacial tunnel oxide passivating contacts for silicon and perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells with improved efficiency
